title: Streaming structured JSON: escape/truncate/retry edge cases and SDK parser updates
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket tracks a focused engineering effort to harden streaming structured JSON outputs for the Redwood Core API and SDKs. We are seeing edge cases where streaming partial JSON tokens, unexpected quoting/escaping, server-side truncation, or retries during tool/function-calls can cause: (a) parsers to emit invalid JSON, (b) duplicated tool invocations on retry, or (c) silent data loss when truncation removes closing braces.

Problem areas observed:
- Delta streaming sends string fragments that contain bare quotation marks and control characters; naive parsers attempt to assemble and fail to unescape correctly.
- When responses are truncated by server (size quotas, abrupt connection close), the last JSON object is left incomplete. Current clients often treat partial data as fatal.
- Retries during streaming (network reconnects, HTTP proxy retries) can replay the same tool call; some tool servers are not idempotent.
- Existing compatibility layers (older SDK versions) expect newline-delimited JSON objects; we now stream nested structures (arrays/objects across multiple deltas) which breaks older parsers.

Goals:
1. Define a wire-safe streaming protocol extension for structured JSON deltas that keeps backwards compatibility for line-delimited readers while enabling robust resumable parsing.
2. Update server behavior to tag deltas with sequence numbers and checksum metadata and emit explicit truncation markers when server-side truncation occurs.
3. Change SDK streaming parsers (JS/Python/Go) to support: incremental JSON assembly with seq numbers, escaped content handling (UTF-8 safe), resumable reconnection using last-ack seq, and idempotency tokens for tool/function calls to prevent duplicate execution.
4. Add integration tests and fuzz tests that simulate truncated streams, injected escapes, and retry scenarios.

Proposed protocol rules (implementation work tracked here):
- Each streaming delta is a JSON envelope string with the following fields (server guarantees these fields are present in streaming mode):
  - "seq": integer sequence number (monotonic within response)
  - "type": one of ["delta","meta","truncation","final"]
  - "payload": string (string-escaped chunk of the logical JSON body)
  - "checksum": base64(SHA256) for the cumulative payload up to seq (optional for early deltas, required for final)
  - "idempotency_token": string (only present on initial messages that trigger tool/function-calls)
- Escaping: payload is a JSON string; servers must JSON-escape any control chars. Binary blobs are base64-encoded and clearly labeled in payload_type.
- Truncation: if server must cut a response, it emits a "truncation" envelope with "truncation_hint" and a boolean "truncated": true. This allows clients to present a graceful user-facing message and optionally request a full non-streamed fallback.
- Reconnect/resume: client reconnects with last-seen seq and checksum; server may resume at next seq or respond with a new full response. If the original stream initiated a tool call, client must resend idempotency_token to indicate it has already been handled; server must honor token to avoid re-execution.

Backward compatibility decisions:
- Line-delimited JSON consumers: server will continue to emit a stable newline-delimited top-level envelope per delta so older clients can at least parse per-envelope events. However, nested JSON assembly across multiple deltas is a new feature that older SDKs will ignore.
- For older SDKs, we will add a server-side flag in the first meta envelope: "compat_mode": "ndjson" to preserve strict NDJSON behavior for legacy consumers.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for SDK incremental parser: valid multi-delta assembly, malformed escape sequences, finalization on truncation envelope.
- Integration tests that spin up a mock tool server that increments counters on invocation; ensure idempotency_token prevents double-execution across retries.
- Chaos tests in CI that simulate connection reset after random seq; verify resume logic and checksum validation.
- Fuzz tests that inject control characters and unicode separators to validate escape handling.

Rollout plan:
1. Server: implement envelope fields + truncation marker behind feature flag "streaming-structured-v2". Canary to 5% of hosted customers with opt-in.
2. SDKs: release parsers with opt-in mode enabled by default for latest SDKs (JS/Python/Go). Document migration steps for older clients.
3. Monitor: add telemetry for truncation events, resume success rates, and idempotency token mismatches (dashboards: STREAMING/structured/v2).
4. Gradual ramp to 100% after 4 weeks of canary with no regressions.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should server include cumulative JSON length or rely on checksum? (checksum chosen to avoid off-bytes issues across encodings.)
- Where to store idempotency-token state for Private deployments (we propose a TTL-backed in-memory store with optional durable backing).
- UX when truncation occurs: offer fallback full-response fetch or present a truncated view? (Plan: SDK exposes a helper that calls /responses/{id}/full if truncation detected.)

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Streaming+Structured+JSON+V2
- RFC: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/streaming-structured-json-rfc
- PoC PR (server): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-server/pull/1248

2026-03-03 — Security (Evan Cho): idempotency_token storage design reviewed; recommended TTL of 24h and rotation. No blocking issues.
2026-03-04 — Marco Li: SDK parsers updated in branch sdk-streaming-parser. Added resume logic using seq+checksum. Unit tests green locally, integration flaky under proxy; investigating.

notes: Implementation must avoid changing existing NDJSON consumers unless feature-flagged.
Tool/function calling flows must carry idempotency_token; add server validations for duplicate tokens.
Add metrics: streaming.resume_attempts, streaming.resume_success_rate, streaming.truncation_count, streaming.idempotency_conflicts.
